title: Add and Search Word
prompt:
The classic version of this problem defines a `WordDictionary` class supporting interleaved `addWord` and `search` calls. Since this test harness calls a single pure function per test case rather than exercising a stateful object, we adapt it: implement `add_search_word(words_to_add, queries)`.

First, insert every word in `words_to_add` into a trie (all insertions happen up front). Then, for each pattern in `queries`, determine whether it matches any word in the trie, where a `.` in the pattern can match any single letter. Return a list of booleans, one per query, in order.

A pattern matches a word if they're the same length and every non-`.` character in the pattern equals the corresponding character in the word.

examples.explanation: "pad" matches no inserted word. "bad" matches exactly. ".ad" matches "bad", "dad", or "mad" (any letter in the first slot). "b.." matches "bad" (any letters in slots 2 and 3).
"a" matches exactly, "." matches "a" via wildcard, "aa" doesn't match since lengths differ.

constraints: words_to_add[i] consists of lowercase English letters
queries[i] consists of lowercase English letters and/or '.'
At most 2 dots appear in any single query
hints: Build a standard trie from words_to_add first, where each node maps a character to a child node and tracks whether a word ends there.
Searching a pattern is a normal trie walk EXCEPT when you hit a '.': since it can match any letter, you must try every child at that position, recursively continuing the search from each one.

Write the search as a recursive helper taking (pattern, index, current node). At a '.', loop over all children of the current node and return true if any recursive branch succeeds; otherwise, follow the single matching character as usual.

solution.approach: Build a trie by inserting every word in words_to_add up front, exactly as in a standard trie: each node has a dict of children keyed by character and a flag marking word endings. For searching, use a recursive function that walks the pattern character by character against a current trie node. On a normal letter, follow the matching child if it exists, or fail. On a '.', since it can represent any letter, branch into every child of the current node and return true if any branch leads to a full match. A match succeeds when we've consumed the whole pattern and the current node is marked as a word ending.
solution.timeComplexity: O(total characters inserted) for building, and O(26^d * L) worst case per query with d dots and length L
